objects.description: C++ exception class used by OpenCV to report errors (code, message, function, file, line). Overrides std::exception::what(). Constructed internally via OpenCV error macros.
Principal Component Analysis utility for dimensionality reduction and projection/back-projection, with methods to compute from data and store mean/eigenvectors/eigenvalues.
Linear Discriminant Analysis class for supervised dimensionality reduction and projection/reconstruction.
Singular Value Decomposition utility class with in-place and static compute/back substitution methods, storing U, W, VT matrices.
Pseudo-random number generator (Multiply-With-Carry) providing scalar draws, distributions, array filling, and Gaussian draws.
Mersenne Twister 19937 generator wrapper with typical sampling utilities.
Abstract iterator interface used by Formatter to stream formatted matrix text chunks.
Abstract formatting strategy to render cv::Mat into various textual formats (Matlab, CSV, etc.).
Base class for OpenCV algorithms providing I/O (read/write/save), factory loading helpers, and lifecycle hooks.
2D Delaunay triangulation and Voronoi diagram structure with insertion, location, and topology navigation utilities.
Abstract interface for the LSD (Line Segment Detector) with methods to detect and render line segments.
Interface for Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization algorithm over tiles. Implementations are created via createCLAHE.
Abstract Generalized Hough transform interfaces: base class with configuration and detect; Ballard variant (position only); Guil variant (position, rotation, scale).
Utility to iterate across pixels along a discrete line segment with 4/8 connectivity; can operate with or without an image buffer (point mode).

functions.name: cv::error
functions.signature: void cv::error(const cv::Exception& exc)
functions.description: Signals an OpenCV error and raises an exception. By default prints the error information to stderr and then throws cv::Exception unless cv::setBreakOnError() was enabled or a custom handler was installed via redirectError(). Deprecated overload.
requirements: exc must be a valid cv::Exception object with properly initialized fields (code, err, func, file, line).
Throws (CV_NORETURN) – callers should not expect this function to return; control flow ends here.

functions.name: cv::error
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS CV_NORETURN void error(const Exception& exc);
functions.description: Signals an error: prints info and either aborts if break-on-error is set or throws given Exception. Deprecated overload.
requirements: Provide a constructed cv::Exception.

functions.name: cv::swap
functions.signature: void cv::swap(cv::Mat& a, cv::Mat& b)
functions.description: Swaps two cv::Mat header/data handles efficiently (no element-wise moves). Useful to exchange matrix contents in O(1) time.
requirements: a and b may alias the same underlying data; swap will exchange headers and, if needed, allocator handles.
Both Mat objects must be valid (constructed).

functions.name: cv::borderInterpolate
functions.signature: int cv::borderInterpolate(int p, int len, int borderType)
functions.description: Computes the source index for an out-of-range coordinate p given an array length len and a border extrapolation mode (BorderTypes). Returns -1 for BORDER_CONSTANT.
requirements: len must be > 0.
borderType must be a valid cv::BorderTypes except BORDER_TRANSPARENT and BORDER_ISOLATED.
When borderType == BORDER_CONSTANT the function always returns -1.

functions.name: cv::copyMakeBorder
functions.signature: void cv::copyMakeBorder(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, int top, int bottom, int left, int right, int borderType, const cv::Scalar& value = cv::Scalar())
functions.description: Forms a border around an image by copying src into the center of dst and filling margins according to borderType or with constant value. Used to prepare images for algorithms that need explicit padding.
requirements: src must be a valid array (any depth/channels supported by OpenCV).
dst will be created as type(src) and size (src.rows+top+bottom, src.cols+left+right).
top, bottom, left, right must be >= 0.
borderType must be a valid cv::BorderTypes; use value only with BORDER_CONSTANT.
If src is ROI and you want pure extrapolation, use borderType | BORDER_ISOLATED.

functions.name: cv::add
functions.signature: void cv::add(cv::InputArray src1, cv::InputArray src2, cv::OutputArray dst, cv::InputArray mask = cv::noArray(), int dtype = -1)
functions.description: Per-element sum of two arrays or an array and a scalar (broadcast). Optionally applies an 8U mask and allows output depth override via dtype.
requirements: src1 and src2 must be same size and same number of channels unless one is a scalar.
dtype = -1 means dst depth equals input(s) depth; otherwise dst depth must be compatible.
If mask provided: type CV_8U single-channel, same size as inputs.
No saturation for CV_32S outputs (may overflow with unexpected sign).

functions.name: cv::subtract
functions.signature: void cv::subtract(cv::InputArray src1, cv::InputArray src2, cv::OutputArray dst, cv::InputArray mask = cv::noArray(), int dtype = -1)
functions.description: Per-element difference: dst = src1 - src2 with optional mask and output depth control. Supports array–array and array–scalar forms.
requirements: src1 and src2: same size and channels unless one is a scalar.
mask, if used: CV_8U single-channel, same size.
dtype rules as in cv::add.
No saturation for CV_32S outputs.

functions.name: cv::multiply
functions.signature: void cv::multiply(cv::InputArray src1, cv::InputArray src2, cv::OutputArray dst, double scale = 1, int dtype = -1)
functions.description: Per-element product (optionally scaled) of two arrays. Supports array–scalar via broadcasting.
requirements: src1 and src2 must be same size and type (channels and depth) unless scalar used.
scale is applied after multiplication.
dtype can override output depth; if -1, output same depth as inputs.
No saturation for CV_32S outputs.

functions.name: cv::divide
functions.signature: void cv::divide(cv::InputArray src1, cv::InputArray src2, cv::OutputArray dst, double scale = 1, int dtype = -1)
functions.description: Per-element division: dst = saturate(src1*scale / src2). Multi-channel processed independently. Integer division by zero produces zero; floating point uses IEEE-754 (Inf/NaN).
requirements: src1 and src2: same size and type unless scalar used.
dtype = -1 allowed only when src1.depth()==src2.depth() for array/array division; otherwise specify output depth.
For integer outputs, division by zero yields 0.
No saturation for CV_32S outputs.

functions.name: cv::scaleAdd
functions.signature: void cv::scaleAdd(cv::InputArray src1, double alpha, cv::InputArray src2, cv::OutputArray dst)
functions.description: Computes dst = alpha*src1 + src2 (DAXPY/SAXPY). All arrays same size and type.
requirements: src1 and src2 must be same size and type; dst same size and type as src1.
alpha is applied in src1’s element type precision (use double for max precision).

functions.name: cv::addWeighted
functions.signature: void cv::addWeighted(cv::InputArray src1, double alpha, cv::InputArray src2, double beta, double gamma, cv::OutputArray dst, int dtype = -1)
functions.description: Weighted sum of two arrays plus scalar: dst = saturate(src1*alpha + src2*beta + gamma).
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and number of channels.
dtype=-1 uses input depth; otherwise specify valid output depth.
No saturation for CV_32S outputs.

functions.name: cv::convertScaleAbs
functions.signature: void cv::convertScaleAbs(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, double alpha = 1, double beta = 0)
functions.description: Scales src by alpha, adds beta, takes absolute value, and converts to 8-bit unsigned (uchar) with saturate_cast.
requirements: dst will be CV_8U with same size and channels as src.
alpha and beta are applied per element before abs and cast.

functions.name: cv::convertFp16
functions.signature: void cv::convertFp16(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst)
functions.description: Converts between FP32 and FP16 representations (using CV_16S container for FP16). Deprecated in favor of Mat::convertTo with CV_16F.
requirements: src type must be CV_32F or CV_16S (FP16 container); otherwise an error is raised.
dst type becomes the complementary type (FP16<->FP32).

functions.name: cv::LUT
functions.signature: void cv::LUT(cv::InputArray src, cv::InputArray lut, cv::OutputArray dst)
functions.description: Applies a lookup table transform: for integer src, uses shifted index mapping per depth. Supports 8U/8S/16U/16S sources and 256 or 65536 table size; handles multi-channel arrays with per-channel or shared LUT.
requirements: src must be 8-bit or 16-bit integer type (CV_8U, CV_8S, CV_16U, CV_16S).
lut must have 256 entries for 8-bit depths or 65536 for 16-bit depths; channels either 1 or match src.channels().
dst same size and number of channels as src; depth equals lut.depth().

functions.name: cv::sum
functions.signature: cv::Scalar cv::sum(cv::InputArray src)
functions.description: Computes per-channel sum of all elements of src and returns as Scalar (up to 4 channels).
requirements: src must have 1 to 4 channels.
For large arrays, sums may overflow for small integer types; prefer float/double inputs for safety.

functions.name: cv::hasNonZero
functions.signature: bool cv::hasNonZero(cv::InputArray src)
functions.description: Returns true if there is at least one non-zero element in a single-channel array.
requirements: src must be single-channel. For multi-channel arrays, reshape or extract a channel before calling.

functions.name: cv::countNonZero
functions.signature: int cv::countNonZero(cv::InputArray src)
functions.description: Counts the number of non-zero elements in a single-channel array.
requirements: src must be single-channel (use reshape/extract channel for multi-channel data).

functions.name: cv::findNonZero
functions.signature: void cv::findNonZero(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray idx)
functions.description: Finds locations of non-zero pixels in a single-channel binary or general single-channel array. Returns either Mat of Points or std::vector<Point> via OutputArray.
requirements: src must be single-channel (binary or general).
idx must be an OutputArray that can hold cv::Mat of cv::Point or std::vector<cv::Point>.
Order of points is implementation-defined.

functions.name: cv::mean
functions.signature: cv::Scalar cv::mean(cv::InputArray src, cv::InputArray mask = cv::noArray())
functions.description: Computes per-channel mean (average) over all elements (optionally masked) and returns as Scalar.
requirements: src must have 1 to 4 channels.
mask, if provided, must be CV_8U single-channel same size as src (non-zero selects elements).

functions.name: cv::meanStdDev
functions.signature: void cv::meanStdDev(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray mean, cv::OutputArray stddev, cv::InputArray mask = cv::noArray())
functions.description: Computes per-channel mean and standard deviation of src (optionally masked).
requirements: src must have 1 to 4 channels.
mean and stddev must accept Scalar-like outputs (typically CV_64F).
mask, if provided, CV_8U single-channel same size as src.

functions.name: cv::norm
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double norm(InputArray src1, int normType = NORM_L2, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Computes a vector/matrix norm of a single array. Supports L1/L2/Inf and Hamming (with type constraints). Use mask to restrict computation to a region.
requirements: src1 must be a valid cv::InputArray (e.g., Mat, UMat, etc.).
normType must be a valid cv::NormTypes value; Hamming norms require CV_8U depth.
If mask is provided, it must be CV_8UC1 with the same size as src1 and will restrict the region used for norm computation.

functions.name: cv::PSNR
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double PSNR(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, double R=255.);
functions.description: Computes the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) between two arrays of equal size/type, in dB.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have the same size and type.
R is the maximum signal value for the depth (e.g., 255 for CV_8U).

functions.name: cv::batchDistance
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void batchDistance(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dist, int dtype, OutputArray nidx, int normType = NORM_L2, int K = 0, InputArray mask = noArray(), int update = 0, bool crosscheck = false);
functions.description: Naive nearest-neighbor/batch distance computation between rows of src1 and src2 using given norm; can output distances and neighbor indices (nidx).
requirements: src1 and src2 must be compatible in type and feature dimension (same number of columns if treating rows as samples).
dtype specifies output depth for dist.
normType must be compatible; Hamming requires CV_8U.
If K > 0, the function returns K nearest neighbors in nidx and associated distances in dist.
If mask is provided, it must be CV_8UC1 and shape must align with compared pairs as per OpenCV conventions (unspecified details beyond standard API).
crosscheck toggles mutual best match requirement; update parameter controls internal updates (unspecified details).

functions.name: cv::normalize
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void normalize(InputArray src, InputOutputArray dst, double alpha = 1, double beta = 0, int norm_type = NORM_L2, int dtype = -1, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Normalizes an array by scale-and-shift to a target norm (L1/L2/Inf) or maps values to a range [alpha,beta] when norm_type==NORM_MINMAX. mask restricts region used for stats and modified output.
requirements: src must be a valid array; multi-channel supported with type-dependent behavior.
dst must be preallocated or will be created; dtype controls output depth (-1 to keep source depth).
When norm_type==NORM_MINMAX, operates on dense arrays; mask (if provided) must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src.
Range mode (MINMAX) is not allowed for sparse matrices.

functions.name: cv::minMaxLoc
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void minMaxLoc(InputArray src, double* minVal, double* maxVal = 0, Point* minLoc = 0, Point* maxLoc = 0, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Finds global minimum/maximum values and their locations in a single-channel array; supports mask to restrict search. For multi-channel inputs in C++, omit loc/mask.
requirements: src must be single-channel for use with loc/mask in C++; in Python multi-channel not supported.
mask (if provided) must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src.
Pointers (minVal/maxVal/minLoc/maxLoc) can be NULL to skip.

functions.name: cv::reduceArgMin
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void reduceArgMin(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int axis, bool lastIndex = false);
functions.description: Along the given axis, computes indices of minimum elements for each slice. Returns indices as CV_32SC1 of same dimensionality with axis reduced to size 1.
requirements: src must be single-channel array.
axis must be in [0, src.dims).
dst will be CV_32SC1; function may create internal copy if arrays are not continuous.
NaN handling is unspecified; returned index is guaranteed in bounds.

functions.name: cv::reduceArgMax
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void reduceArgMax(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int axis, bool lastIndex = false);
functions.description: Along the given axis, computes indices of maximum elements for each slice. Returns indices as CV_32SC1.
requirements: src must be single-channel array.
axis must be in [0, src.dims).
dst will be CV_32SC1; may copy non-continuous data.
NaN handling is unspecified; returned index is guaranteed in bounds.

functions.name: cv::minMaxIdx
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void minMaxIdx(InputArray src, double* minVal, double* maxVal = 0, int* minIdx = 0, int* maxIdx = 0, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Finds global min/max values and nD indices in a single-channel array; supports mask for dense arrays. For sparse arrays, uses only non-zero elements (see overload).
requirements: src must be single-channel.
If mask is provided, it must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src.
minIdx/maxIdx arrays (if provided) must have src.dims elements each.

functions.name: cv::reduce
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void reduce(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int dim, int rtype, int dtype = -1);
functions.description: Reduces a 2D matrix to a vector by applying a reduction (sum/avg/min/max/sum2) along rows (dim=0) or columns (dim=1).
requirements: src must be 2D; multi-channel allowed with constraints per rtype.
dim must be 0 (reduce rows) or 1 (reduce cols).
rtype must be one of cv::ReduceTypes.
If dtype < 0, dst has same type as src; otherwise dst depth follows dtype and channels match src.

functions.name: cv::merge
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void merge(const Mat* mv, size_t count, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Creates a multi-channel array by merging several single-channel Mat arrays in mv[0..count-1].
requirements: All input matrices must have the same size and depth and be single-channel.
count must be > 0.
dst will have number of channels equal to count.

functions.name: cv::split
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void split(const Mat& src, Mat* mvbegin);
functions.description: Splits a multi-channel Mat into separate single-channel Mat outputs written to a C-array starting at mvbegin.
requirements: src must have multiple channels.
The output array must have at least src.channels() elements; each output Mat will be reallocated if needed.

functions.name: cv::mixChannels
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void mixChannels(const Mat* src, size_t nsrcs, Mat* dst, size_t ndsts, const int* fromTo, size_t npairs);
functions.description: Copies specified channels from input arrays to specified channels of pre-allocated output arrays according to fromTo pairs.
requirements: All src matrices must have same size and depth.
All dst matrices must be pre-allocated with same size and depth as src[0].
fromTo must contain 2*npairs integers mapping input-channel index to output-channel index in continuous channel numbering.
npairs defines number of channel mappings.

functions.name: cv::extractChannel
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void extractChannel(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int coi);
functions.description: Extracts a single channel (0-based index) from src into dst.
requirements: coi must be in [0, src.channels()-1].
dst will be single-channel with same size and depth as src.

functions.name: cv::insertChannel
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void insertChannel(InputArray src, InputOutputArray dst, int coi);
functions.description: Inserts a single-channel src into channel index coi of multi-channel dst.
requirements: dst must be multi-channel and pre-allocated with same size and depth as src.
coi must be in [0, dst.channels()-1].
src must be single-channel and same size/depth as dst.

functions.name: cv::flip
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void flip(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flipCode);
functions.description: Flips a 2D array around x-axis (flipCode=0), y-axis (>0), or both axes (<0).
requirements: src must be 2D; dst will be same size and type as src.
flipCode determines axis as specified.

functions.name: cv::flipND
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void flipND(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int axis);
functions.description: Flips an n-dimensional array along a given axis (0 <= axis < src.dims).
requirements: axis must be in range [0, src.dims).
dst will have same shape/type as src.

functions.name: cv::broadcast
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void broadcast(InputArray src, InputArray shape, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Broadcasts src to a target shape; shape is a list (array) of CV_32S numbers; negative values are not supported.
requirements: shape must be an array of CV_32S with desired dimensions; values must be non-negative.
Broadcasting semantics require src to be singleton or matching along respective dimensions.

functions.name: cv::rotate
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void rotate(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int rotateCode);
functions.description: Rotates a 2D array by multiples of 90 degrees using RotateFlags (90 CW, 180, 90 CCW).
requirements: src must be 2D.
dst will be same type; size updated according to rotation (swap rows/cols for 90-degree rotations).
rotateCode must be one of cv::RotateFlags.

functions.name: cv::repeat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void repeat(InputArray src, int ny, int nx, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Tiles src ny times vertically and nx times horizontally into dst.
requirements: ny and nx must be positive integers.
dst will have same type as src and size (src.rows*ny, src.cols*nx).

functions.name: cv::hconcat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void hconcat(const Mat* src, size_t nsrc, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Horizontally concatenates nsrc matrices with same number of rows and same depth into dst.
requirements: All src matrices must have same number of rows and same depth; types may differ only in channel count but depth must match.
dst will have rows equal to input rows and columns equal to sum of input cols.

functions.name: cv::vconcat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void vconcat(const Mat* src, size_t nsrc, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Vertically concatenates nsrc matrices with same number of columns and same depth into dst.
requirements: All src matrices must have same number of columns and same depth.
dst columns = columns of inputs; rows = sum of input rows.

functions.name: cv::bitwise_and
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void bitwise_and(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Computes per-element bitwise AND between two arrays or array and scalar; mask restricts write.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type when both arrays; scalar forms require appropriate construction via cv::Scalar.
mask (if provided) must be CV_8UC1 and same size as inputs.
Floating point arrays operate on bitwise representation.

functions.name: cv::bitwise_or
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void bitwise_or(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Per-element bitwise OR with same constraints as bitwise_and.
requirements: src1/src2 same size and type; mask is CV_8UC1 if used.

functions.name: cv::bitwise_xor
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void bitwise_xor(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Per-element bitwise XOR with same constraints as bitwise_and.
requirements: src1/src2 same size and type; mask is CV_8UC1 if used.

functions.name: cv::bitwise_not
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void bitwise_not(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Per-element bitwise inversion of src; mask can restrict write to dst.
requirements: mask (if provided) must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src.

functions.name: cv::absdiff
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void absdiff(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Per-element absolute difference between two arrays or array and scalar (via cv::Scalar wrapper).
requirements: src1 and src2 must have broadcast-compatible size/type per OpenCV rules; typically same size and type.

functions.name: cv::copyTo
functions.signature: void CV_EXPORTS_W copyTo(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask);
functions.description: Copies src to dst using optional mask; if dst is reallocated, new memory is zero-initialized before masked copy (Python-convenience overload).
requirements: mask must be same size as src; type CV_8U (single or multiple channels per note).
dst will be reallocated to src size/type if not matching.

functions.name: cv::inRange
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void inRange(InputArray src, InputArray lowerb, InputArray upperb, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Checks whether elements of src lie within inclusive ranges [lowerb, upperb] per channel; outputs CV_8U mask (255 where in-range, 0 otherwise).
requirements: src must be single or multi-channel; lowerb/upperb are arrays or scalars matching src channels.
dst will be CV_8U same size as src.

functions.name: cv::compare
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void compare(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, int cmpop);
functions.description: Per-element comparison producing CV_8U mask (255 where true); supports array-array and array-scalar forms.
requirements: When arrays, src1 and src2 must be single-channel and same size/type.
cmpop must be one of cv::CmpTypes.
dst type is CV_8U with same size and channel count as inputs.

functions.name: cv::min
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void min(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Per-element minimum of two arrays or array and scalar (via cv::Scalar wrapper) into dst.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type when arrays; scalar forms constructed appropriately.
dst has same size and type as inputs.

functions.name: cv::max
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void max(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Per-element maximum of two arrays or array and scalar (via cv::Scalar wrapper).
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type when arrays; scalar forms constructed appropriately.

functions.name: cv::sqrt
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void sqrt(InputArray src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Computes per-element square root; multi-channel processed independently. Accurate as std::sqrt for given depth.
requirements: src must be floating-point (recommended); dst same size/type as src.

functions.name: cv::pow
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void pow(InputArray src, double power, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Raises each element of src to given power; for non-integer power uses abs(src) to avoid complex results. Special values (NaN/Inf) not handled.
requirements: dst same size/type as src.
Note: for negative values and non-integer powers, sign is not preserved unless additional steps (see docs).

functions.name: cv::exp
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void exp(InputArray src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Per-element natural exponent e^(src); denormals may be flushed to zero; NaN/Inf not handled specially.
requirements: src and dst are same size/type; floating-point types recommended.

functions.name: cv::log
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void log(InputArray src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Per-element natural logarithm; output on zero/negative/NaN/Inf is undefined.
requirements: Inputs should be positive floats for defined results; dst same size/type as src.

functions.name: cv::polarToCart
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void polarToCart(InputArray magnitude, InputArray angle, OutputArray x, OutputArray y, bool angleInDegrees = false);
functions.description: Converts magnitude and angle arrays to Cartesian x and y coordinates; angles can be radians or degrees.
requirements: If magnitude is empty, behaves as magnitude=1; otherwise magnitude and angle must have same size/type (floating-point).
x and y will be same size/type as angle.

functions.name: cv::cartToPolar
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void cartToPolar(InputArray x, InputArray y, OutputArray magnitude, OutputArray angle, bool angleInDegrees = false);
functions.description: Computes magnitude and angle of 2D vectors from x and y components; outputs floats with angle in radians or degrees.
requirements: x and y must be single or double precision floating-point arrays with same size/type.
magnitude and angle will be same size/type as x.

functions.name: cv::phase
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void phase(InputArray x, InputArray y, OutputArray angle, bool angleInDegrees = false);
functions.description: Computes rotation angle atan2(y, x) for 2D vectors; outputs angle in radians or degrees.
requirements: x and y must be same size/type; floating-point arrays.
angle will be same size/type as x.

functions.name: cv::magnitude
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void magnitude(InputArray x, InputArray y, OutputArray magnitude);
functions.description: Computes vector magnitude sqrt(x^2 + y^2) per element.
requirements: x and y must be floating-point and same size/type.
magnitude will be same size/type as x.

functions.name: cv::checkRange
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W bool checkRange(InputArray a, bool quiet = true, Point* pos = 0, double minVal = -DBL_MAX, double maxVal = DBL_MAX);
functions.description: Checks that all elements are finite (not NaN/Inf) and within [minVal, maxVal). If out-of-range, returns false (or throws if quiet=false).
requirements: a must be valid array; multi-channel processed per-channel.
If pos is provided, it must point to a Point to receive first outlier position.

functions.name: cv::patchNaNs
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void patchNaNs(InputOutputArray a, double val = 0);
functions.description: Replaces NaN values in-place in a CV_32F or CV_64F matrix with the specified value (default 0).
requirements: a must be CV_32F or CV_64F.
Operation is in-place.

functions.name: cv::gemm
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void gemm(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, double alpha, InputArray src3, double beta, OutputArray dst, int flags = 0);
functions.description: Generalized matrix multiplication: dst = alpha*op(src1)*op(src2) + beta*op(src3) where ops depend on flags (GEMM_1_T etc.). Supports real/complex.
requirements: src1 and src2 must be matrices with compatible sizes for multiplication; src3 (if provided) same size as product.
flags controls transposition of inputs.
Types must be compatible (CV_32F/CV_64F or complex forms).

functions.name: cv::mulTransposed
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void mulTransposed(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, bool aTa, InputArray delta = noArray(), double scale = 1, int dtype = -1);
functions.description: Computes product (src-delta)^T*(src-delta) if aTa=true, else (src-delta)*(src-delta)^T, scaled by 'scale'. Used for covariance-like matrices.
requirements: src must be single-channel matrix; dtype if >=0 must be CV_32F or CV_64F.
If delta is provided: empty (treated zero), same size, or broadcast by repetition to src size.

functions.name: cv::transpose
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void transpose(InputArray src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Transposes 2D matrix (no conjugation for complex).
requirements: src must be 2D; dst will be transposed with same type.

functions.name: cv::transposeND
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void transposeND(InputArray src, const std::vector<int>& order, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Permutes N-D axes according to 'order'; input must be continuous single-channel.
requirements: src must be continuous and single-channel; order must be a permutation of 0..N-1.
dst same type; shape permuted.

functions.name: cv::transform
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void transform(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, InputArray m);
functions.description: Applies linear transform to each N-channel element using MxN or Mx(N+1) matrix (affine per-element). Useful for color space transforms or vector transforms.
requirements: src must have channels N equal to m.cols or m.cols-1.
m must be 2x2 or 2x3 for 2D case per docs (general: MxN or Mx(N+1)).
dst will have same size/depth as src with channels = m.rows.

functions.name: cv::perspectiveTransform
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void perspectiveTransform(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, InputArray m);
functions.description: Applies 3x3 (2D) or 4x4 (3D) homogeneous perspective transform to each 2D/3D vector element and divides by w.
requirements: src must be two- or three-channel floating-point array.
m must be 3x3 (2D) or 4x4 (3D) floating-point matrix.
dst same size/type as src.

functions.name: cv::completeSymm
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void completeSymm(InputOutputArray m, bool lowerToUpper = false);
functions.description: Copies one triangular half of a square matrix to the other to make it symmetric; diagonal unchanged.
requirements: m must be square floating-point matrix.
If lowerToUpper=true, copies lower to upper; else upper to lower.

functions.name: cv::setIdentity
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void setIdentity(InputOutputArray mtx, const Scalar& s = Scalar(1));
functions.description: Sets a matrix to a scaled identity: diagonal elements = s, others zero; works for non-square matrices (fills min(rows,cols)).
requirements: mtx must be reallocated or existing; operation writes diagonal.

functions.name: cv::determinant
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double determinant(InputArray mtx);
functions.description: Returns determinant of a square floating-point matrix (small sizes direct; larger via LU).
requirements: mtx must be square and type CV_32F or CV_64F single-channel.

functions.name: cv::trace
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W Scalar trace(InputArray mtx);
functions.description: Returns sum of diagonal elements of a matrix as a Scalar (per-channel trace if multi-channel?).
requirements: mtx must be a valid matrix.

functions.name: cv::invert
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double invert(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flags = DECOMP_LU);
functions.description: Inverts matrix src into dst (or pseudo-inverse) using specified method (LU/SVD/Cholesky). Returns non-zero or condition number depending on method.
requirements: src must be floating-point MxN; method constraints apply (Cholesky requires square symmetric positive-definite).
dst will be NxM same type as src.

functions.name: cv::solve
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W bool solve(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, int flags = DECOMP_LU);
functions.description: Solves linear system src1 * X = src2 (exact or least-squares) using specified decomposition. Writes solution to dst.
requirements: src1 is left-hand matrix; src2 is right-hand; dimensions must conform.
flags one of cv::DecompTypes; DECOMP_NORMAL for normal equations.

functions.name: cv::sort
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void sort(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flags);
functions.description: Sorts each row or column ascending/descending based on flags (SortFlags).
requirements: src must be single-channel.
flags combine SORT_EVERY_ROW/SORT_EVERY_COLUMN with SORT_ASCENDING/SORT_DESCENDING.

functions.name: cv::sortIdx
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void sortIdx(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flags);
functions.description: Sorts each row/column as in sort but writes indices of sorted order to dst (integer).
requirements: src single-channel.
dst integer array same size as src.
flags as in sort.

functions.name: cv::solveCubic
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W int solveCubic(InputArray coeffs, OutputArray roots);
functions.description: Finds real roots of a cubic equation defined by coeffs (size 3 or 4), writes 0–3 roots, returns count (or -1 for all real numbers).
requirements: coeffs must contain 3 or 4 coefficients as documented.
roots is output of 0–3 elements (real roots only).

functions.name: cv::solvePoly
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double solvePoly(InputArray coeffs, OutputArray roots, int maxIters = 300);
functions.description: Finds real and complex roots of a polynomial; roots returned as complex (2-channel). Returns max absolute error.
requirements: coeffs is array of coefficients; roots is output array of complex roots.
maxIters controls iterations.

functions.name: cv::eigen
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W bool eigen(InputArray src, OutputArray eigenvalues, OutputArray eigenvectors = noArray());
functions.description: Computes eigenvalues (and optionally eigenvectors) of a symmetric matrix (src^T == src). Values are sorted descending.
requirements: src must be square CV_32F or CV_64F and symmetric.
eigenvalues is vector; eigenvectors same size/type as src with eigenvectors in rows.

functions.name: cv::eigenNonSymmetric
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void eigenNonSymmetric(InputArray src, OutputArray eigenvalues, OutputArray eigenvectors);
functions.description: Computes real eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a non-symmetric matrix (assumes real eigenvalues).
requirements: src square CV_32F or CV_64F.
Outputs have same type as src; eigenvectors in rows.

functions.name: cv::calcCovarMatrix
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void calcCovarMatrix(const Mat* samples, int nsamples, Mat& covar, Mat& mean, int flags, int ctype = CV_64F);
functions.description: Computes covariance matrix (and optionally mean) of a set of sample vectors provided as separate Mat objects; flags control layout (rows/cols, scrambled/normal, scaling).
requirements: samples must point to nsamples arrays of same vector length; choose flags COVAR_ROWS or COVAR_COLS appropriately.
covar will be square of size matching feature count; mean is input/output depending on flags.
ctype output depth (default CV_64F).

functions.name: cv::PCACompute
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void PCACompute(InputArray data, InputOutputArray mean, OutputArray eigenvectors, int maxComponents = 0);
functions.description: Computes PCA basis (eigenvectors) from data (rows or cols depending on PCA::Flags used elsewhere) keeping up to maxComponents; writes mean and eigenvectors.
requirements: data must be numeric matrix; orientation is indicated when used with PCA::Flags in higher-level calls (wrapped operator).
mean is input/output (use noArray for auto-computed).
maxComponents >= 0.

functions.name: cv::PCAProject
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void PCAProject(InputArray data, InputArray mean, InputArray eigenvectors, OutputArray result);
functions.description: Projects vectors (rows/cols) into PCA subspace defined by mean and eigenvectors.
requirements: mean and eigenvectors must match those produced by PCA of the corresponding data orientation.
result will have coordinate dimension equal to number of eigenvectors.

functions.name: cv::PCABackProject
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void PCABackProject(InputArray data, InputArray mean, InputArray eigenvectors, OutputArray result);
functions.description: Reconstructs vectors from their PCA projections using mean and eigenvectors.
requirements: data must be coordinates in PCA space; mean/eigenvectors consistent with projection basis.

functions.name: cv::SVDecomp
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void SVDecomp(InputArray src, OutputArray w, OutputArray u, OutputArray vt, int flags = 0);
functions.description: Computes Singular Value Decomposition of src: src = U*diag(w)*Vt; flags control computation options (NO_UV/FULL_UV).
requirements: src must be CV_32F or CV_64F.
Output matrices sized accordingly; flags per SVD::Flags.

functions.name: cv::SVBackSubst
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void SVBackSubst(InputArray w, InputArray u, InputArray vt, InputArray rhs, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Solves linear system using precomputed SVD decomposition and right-hand side rhs.
requirements: w,u,vt must come from SVD of A; rhs must have compatible dims for solution.
dst will be solution.

functions.name: cv::Mahalanobis
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double Mahalanobis(InputArray v1, InputArray v2, InputArray icovar);
functions.description: Computes Mahalanobis distance between vectors v1 and v2 given inverse covariance matrix icovar.
requirements: v1 and v2 must be 1D vectors of same length; icovar must be square with matching dimension and be inverse covariance.
Types must be compatible (floating-point).

functions.name: cv::dft
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void dft(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flags = 0, int nonzeroRows = 0);
functions.description: Computes forward/inverse Discrete Fourier Transform of 1D/2D arrays with various output formats controlled by flags (DFT_*, COMPLEX_OUTPUT, REAL_OUTPUT, SCALE, ROWS).
requirements: src must be real or complex array (use two-channel for complex).
nonzeroRows can optimize row-wise transforms.
Efficient sizes via getOptimalDFTSize recommended.

functions.name: cv::idft
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void idft(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flags = 0, int nonzeroRows = 0);
functions.description: Inverse DFT convenience wrapper (equivalent to dft with DFT_INVERSE).
requirements: Same as dft; note scaling is not applied unless DFT_SCALE flag is set.

functions.name: cv::dct
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void dct(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flags = 0);
functions.description: Computes forward/inverse Discrete Cosine Transform (1D/2D) depending on flags (DCT_INVERSE, DCT_ROWS).
requirements: src must be floating-point; even sizes supported; performance depends on size (use getOptimalDFTSize transform for padded sizes).

functions.name: cv::idct
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void idct(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flags = 0);
functions.description: Inverse DCT (equivalent to dct with DCT_INVERSE).
requirements: Same as dct.

functions.name: cv::mulSpectrums
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void mulSpectrums(InputArray a, InputArray b, OutputArray c, int flags, bool conjB = false);
functions.description: Multiplies two Fourier spectra (complex or CCS-packed) per element; optional conjugation of second operand; supports DFT_ROWS.
requirements: a and b must be same size/type representing spectra; c same size/type.
flags either 0 or DFT_ROWS.

functions.name: cv::getOptimalDFTSize
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W int getOptimalDFTSize(int vecsize);
functions.description: Returns smallest N >= vecsize such that N is composed of 2^p * 3^q * 5^r for efficient DFT.
requirements: vecsize must be non-negative; negative returned if too large (near INT_MAX).

functions.name: cv::theRNG
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS RNG& theRNG();
functions.description: Returns reference to thread-local default RNG. Use for fast repeated random number generation.
requirements: None; RNG is per-thread.

functions.name: cv::setRNGSeed
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void setRNGSeed(int seed);
functions.description: Sets the state of the default RNG to a specific seed value.
requirements: Provide deterministic seed as int.

functions.name: cv::randu
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void randu(InputOutputArray dst, InputArray low, InputArray high);
functions.description: Fills dst with uniformly distributed random numbers in [low, high).
requirements: dst must be pre-allocated; supports up to 4 channels.
low/high can be scalars or arrays matching channels; values interpreted per channel type.
For integer types, saturation/clipping per docs.

functions.name: cv::randn
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void randn(InputOutputArray dst, InputArray mean, InputArray stddev);
functions.description: Fills dst with normally distributed random numbers with given mean and stddev (vector or diagonal).
requirements: dst must be pre-allocated (1 to 4 channels).
mean and stddev can be vectors or matrices matching channel layout.

functions.name: cv::randShuffle
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void randShuffle(InputOutputArray dst, double iterFactor = 1., RNG* rng = 0);
functions.description: Randomly shuffles elements of a 1D array in place using swap operations scaled by iterFactor; optionally uses provided RNG.
requirements: dst must be numerical 1D array.
iterFactor controls number of swaps as rows*cols*iterFactor.
rng may be null to use theRNG().

functions.name: cv::kmeans
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double kmeans(InputArray data, int K, InputOutputArray bestLabels, TermCriteria criteria, int attempts, int flags, OutputArray centers = noArray());
functions.description: Performs k-means clustering; returns compactness and outputs bestLabels and optionally centers. Multiple attempts with different initializations supported.
requirements: data must be array of N-D float points (various supported layouts).
K > 1; bestLabels must be integer array sized to number of samples; if KMEANS_USE_INITIAL_LABELS used, initialize bestLabels for first attempt.
criteria controls termination; attempts >=1.
flags choose initialization method (RANDOM/PP) and label use.
centers (if provided) will be K x dims of type CV_32F.

functions.name: cv::Formatter::get
functions.signature: static Ptr<Formatter> get(Formatter::FormatType fmt = FMT_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Returns a formatter object for pretty-printing matrices/arrays (default, MATLAB, CSV, Python, NumPy, C styles).
requirements: fmt must be one of Formatter::FormatType.
Returned Ptr<Formatter> can be used to format Mat via Formatter::format.

functions.name: cv::Algorithm::write
functions.signature: CV_WRAP virtual void write(FileStorage& fs) const;
functions.description: Writes algorithm parameters to a FileStorage; base implementation is no-op (derived classes should override).
requirements: fs must be an open FileStorage in write mode.
Call on a valid Algorithm-derived instance.

functions.name: cv::Algorithm::save
functions.signature: CV_WRAP virtual void save(const String& filename) const;
functions.description: Saves the algorithm to a file by opening FileStorage and calling write; derived class must implement write.
requirements: filename must be writable path.
Object must implement write(FileStorage&).

functions.name: cv::Algorithm::getDefaultName
functions.signature: CV_WRAP virtual String getDefaultName() const;
functions.description: Returns default string identifier used as top-level node tag when saving to FileStorage.
requirements: None; derived classes may override to provide stable names.

functions.name: cv::getGaussianKernel
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W Mat getGaussianKernel(int ksize, double sigma, int ktype = CV_64F);
functions.description: Returns a 1D Gaussian kernel of size ksize and standard deviation sigma, normalized to sum to 1. Type CV_32F or CV_64F.
requirements: ksize must be positive odd integer.
sigma > 0 or if non-positive, computed from ksize.
ktype must be CV_32F or CV_64F.

functions.name: cv::getDerivKernels
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void getDerivKernels(OutputArray kx, OutputArray ky, int dx, int dy, int ksize, bool normalize = false, int ktype = CV_32F);
functions.description: Returns 1D derivative kernels for Sobel or Scharr (if ksize=FILTER_SCHARR).
requirements: dx,dy are derivative orders; for ksize=1 only first/second-order x/y allowed; for Scharr use ksize=FILTER_SCHARR.
ktype CV_32F or CV_64F.
normalize scales coefficients if requested.

functions.name: cv::getGaborKernel
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W Mat getGaborKernel(Size ksize, double sigma, double theta, double lambd, double gamma, double psi = CV_PI*0.5, int ktype = CV_64F);
functions.description: Generates 2D Gabor filter kernel with given parameters; returns CV_32F or CV_64F Mat.
requirements: ksize width/height positive; sigma>0; gamma>0; lambd>0.
ktype CV_32F or CV_64F.

functions.name: cv::morphologyDefaultBorderValue
functions.signature: static inline Scalar morphologyDefaultBorderValue();
functions.description: Returns the default border value for morphology (Scalar::all(DBL_MAX) for erosion, transformed to Scalar::all(-DBL_MAX) for dilation internally).
requirements: Used as borderValue in erode/dilate/morphologyEx when BORDER_CONSTANT.

functions.name: cv::getStructuringElement
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W Mat getStructuringElement(int shape, Size ksize, Point anchor = Point(-1,-1));
functions.description: Creates a structuring element (kernel) of given shape and size for morphology operations; anchor defaults to center.
requirements: shape must be MorphShapes (MORPH_RECT/CROSS/ELLIPSE/DIAMOND).
ksize must have positive dimensions.
anchor inside kernel or (-1,-1) for center.

functions.name: cv::medianBlur
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void medianBlur(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int ksize);
functions.description: Applies median filter with ksize x ksize aperture; denoises while preserving edges.
requirements: ksize must be odd and >1 (e.g., 3,5,7).
For ksize 3 or 5, src depth may be CV_8U, CV_16U, CV_32F; for larger, only CV_8U supported.
dst same size/type as src.

functions.name: cv::GaussianBlur
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void GaussianBlur(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, Size ksize, double sigmaX, double sigmaY = 0, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT, AlgorithmHint hint = cv::ALGO_HINT_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Applies Gaussian filter with given kernel size and sigmas; computes missing sigmas from ksize if zeros. Multi-channel supported.
requirements: ksize dims positive odd or zeros to compute from sigmas.
sigmaX>0; if sigmaY==0, uses sigmaX.
borderType any BorderTypes except BORDER_WRAP.
dst same size/type as src.

functions.name: cv::bilateralFilter
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void bilateralFilter(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int d, double sigmaColor, double sigmaSpace, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Applies bilateral filter that preserves edges while smoothing; non-linear, slow for large d.
requirements: src must be 1- or 3-channel 8U or float; dst same size/type.
d is neighborhood diameter (>0 or if <=0 computed from sigmaSpace).
borderType is a valid BorderTypes.

functions.name: cv::boxFilter
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void boxFilter(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int ddepth, Size ksize, Point anchor = Point(-1,-1), bool normalize = true, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Applies box filter (normalized if normalize=true) with given kernel size and anchor.
requirements: ksize positive; borderType valid (no BORDER_WRAP).
ddepth -1 to use src depth or specific depth.
dst same size as src; type per ddepth.

functions.name: cv::sqrBoxFilter
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void sqrBoxFilter(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int ddepth, Size ksize, Point anchor = Point(-1, -1), bool normalize = true, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Computes sum of squared pixels over the box filter footprint (normalized optionally). Useful for local variance.
requirements: Similar to boxFilter requirements. ddepth=-1 or chosen depth.

functions.name: cv::blur
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void blur(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, Size ksize, Point anchor = Point(-1,-1), int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Normalized box blur convenience wrapper.
requirements: ksize positive; borderType valid (no BORDER_WRAP).

functions.name: cv::stackBlur
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void stackBlur(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, Size ksize);
functions.description: Stack blur implementation approximating Gaussian blur with kernel size ksize (odd, positive). BORDER_REPLICATE is used internally.
requirements: ksize width and height must be positive odd.
src depth: CV_8U, CV_16U, CV_16S, or CV_32F; any channel count.
dst same size/type as src.

functions.name: cv::filter2D
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void filter2D(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int ddepth, InputArray kernel, Point anchor = Point(-1,-1), double delta = 0, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Applies 2D correlation with given kernel (not mirrored); large kernels may use DFT internally.
requirements: kernel is single-channel floating-point; dst ddepth -1 or specific; borderType valid (no BORDER_WRAP).
anchor inside kernel or (-1,-1) for center; delta added to result.

functions.name: cv::sepFilter2D
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void sepFilter2D(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int ddepth, InputArray kernelX, InputArray kernelY, Point anchor = Point(-1,-1), double delta = 0, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Applies separable correlation with row kernelX and column kernelY.
requirements: kernelX/kernelY are 1D floating-point vectors.
Other requirements similar to filter2D.

functions.name: cv::Sobel
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void Sobel(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int ddepth, int dx, int dy, int ksize = 3, double scale = 1, double delta = 0, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Computes image derivatives using Sobel or Scharr (if ksize = FILTER_SCHARR).
requirements: ksize must be 1,3,5,7 or FILTER_SCHARR (-1).
ddepth determines destination depth; for 8-bit input use higher-depth to avoid truncation.
borderType valid (no BORDER_WRAP).

functions.name: cv::spatialGradient
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void spatialGradient(InputArray src, OutputArray dx, OutputArray dy, int ksize = 3, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Computes first-order image derivative in x and y using Sobel with ksize=3.
requirements: ksize must be 3.
borderType must be BORDER_DEFAULT (REFLECT_101) or REPLICATE as supported.

functions.name: cv::Scharr
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void Scharr(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int ddepth, int dx, int dy, double scale = 1, double delta = 0, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Computes first-order derivatives using Scharr operator (3x3).
requirements: dx or dy must be 1 (first order); borderType valid (no BORDER_WRAP).

functions.name: cv::Laplacian
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void Laplacian(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int ddepth, int ksize = 1, double scale = 1, double delta = 0, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT);
functions.description: Computes Laplacian (sum of second derivatives) with Sobel-based or fixed 3x3 kernel.
requirements: ksize must be positive odd; commonly 1 or 3,5,7.
borderType valid (no BORDER_WRAP).

functions.name: cv::Canny
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void Canny(InputArray image, OutputArray edges, double threshold1, double threshold2, int apertureSize = 3, bool L2gradient = false);
functions.description: Finds edges using Canny detector on 8-bit input; uses Sobel with given aperture size and thresholds.
requirements: image must be 8-bit single-channel; edges will be CV_8U mask.
apertureSize odd (3,5,7); L2gradient toggles gradient magnitude computation.

functions.name: cv::cornerMinEigenVal
functions.signature: void cv::cornerMinEigenVal(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int blockSize, int ksize = 3, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT)
functions.description: Computes the minimal eigenvalue of the 2x2 gradient covariance matrix at each pixel for corner detection. Produces a CV_32FC1 response map the same size as src.
requirements: src must be single-channel 8-bit or floating-point.
dst is same size as src and CV_32FC1.
blockSize is neighborhood size (>0).
ksize is Sobel aperture size (typically 3); BORDER_WRAP not supported.
Multi-channel input is not allowed.

functions.name: cv::cornerHarris
functions.signature: void cv::cornerHarris(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int blockSize, int ksize, double k, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT)
functions.description: Computes the Harris corner response at each pixel using gradient covariance matrices. Outputs CV_32FC1 response map.
requirements: src must be single-channel 8-bit or floating-point.
dst same size as src, CV_32FC1.
blockSize > 0 neighborhood size.
ksize Sobel aperture (>0); BORDER_WRAP not supported.
k is Harris free parameter (typ. 0.04).

functions.name: cv::cornerEigenValsAndVecs
functions.signature: void cv::cornerEigenValsAndVecs(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int blockSize, int ksize, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT)
functions.description: Computes eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the 2x2 gradient covariance matrix at each pixel. Stores (lambda1, lambda2, x1, y1, x2, y2) per pixel in a 6-channel CV_32F matrix.
requirements: src must be single-channel 8-bit or floating-point.
dst same size as src, type CV_32FC(6).
blockSize > 0; ksize is Sobel aperture.
BORDER_WRAP not supported.

functions.name: cv::preCornerDetect
functions.signature: void cv::preCornerDetect(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int ksize, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT)
functions.description: Computes a cornerness feature map based on image derivatives (used as a precursor to corner detection).
requirements: src single-channel 8-bit or floating-point.
dst same size as src, CV_32F.
ksize is Sobel aperture size.
BORDER_WRAP not supported.

functions.name: cv::cornerSubPix
functions.signature: void cv::cornerSubPix(InputArray image, InputOutputArray corners, Size winSize, Size zeroZone, TermCriteria criteria)
functions.description: Refines corner locations to sub-pixel accuracy using an iterative method based on image gradients.
requirements: image must be single-channel 8-bit or float.
corners contains initial 2D points (Nx1/Nx2 CV_32F/CV_64F) and is updated in-place.
winSize specifies half window size (>0).
zeroZone can be (-1,-1) or non-negative to exclude center.
criteria defines termination by max iterations and/or epsilon.

functions.name: cv::goodFeaturesToTrack
functions.signature: void cv::goodFeaturesToTrack(InputArray image, OutputArray corners, int maxCorners, double qualityLevel, double minDistance, InputArray mask = noArray(), int blockSize = 3, bool useHarrisDetector = false, double k = 0.04)
functions.description: Finds up to maxCorners strongest corners (Shi-Tomasi or Harris) with non-max suppression and minimum spacing.
requirements: image must be single-channel 8-bit or CV_32F.
maxCorners > 0 to limit returned points; <=0 returns all.
qualityLevel in (0,1] is multiplied by best corner measure to threshold.
minDistance >= 0 controls spacing.
mask (if provided) must be 8UC1 same size as image.
blockSize > 0. If useHarrisDetector true, k is Harris parameter.

functions.name: cv::HoughLines
functions.signature: void cv::HoughLines(InputArray image, OutputArray lines, double rho, double theta, int threshold, double srn = 0, double stn = 0, double min_theta = 0, double max_theta = CV_PI, bool use_edgeval = false)
functions.description: Standard/multi-scale Hough transform for lines on a binary edge image; outputs (rho, theta) (and optionally votes).
requirements: image must be 8-bit single-channel binary (non-zero treated as edges).
rho > 0 (distance resolution), theta > 0 (angle resolution).
threshold > 0 votes needed.
If srn, stn > 0 then multi-scale Hough is used; else classical.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces interesting arbitrary strings suitable for OpenCV text APIs
# like putText and getTextSize. It aims to cover diverse Unicode ranges, control
# characters, whitespace patterns, and typical/edge cases, while keeping length reasonable.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

# Collections of character sets to combine
ASCII_PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
WHITESPACES = " \t\n\r\v\f\u00A0\u1680\u2000\u2001\u2002\u2003\u2004\u2005\u2006\u2007\u2008\u2009\u200A\u202F\u205F\u3000\u200B\u200C\u200D\u2060\uFEFF"
CONTROL_ASCII = ''.join(chr(c) for c in list(range(0x00, 0x20)) + [0x7F])
CJK = ''.join([chr(c) for c in range(0x4E00, 0x4F80)])  # subset of CJK Unified Ideographs
EMOJI = [
    "😀","😁","😂","🤣","😃","😄","😅","😆","😉","😊","🙂","🙃","😍","😘","😜","🤔","🤨","😐","😑","😶",
    "🙄","😏","😣","😥","😮","🤐","😯","😪","😫","🥱","😴","😌","😛","😝","🤗","🤭","🤫","🤥",
    "👋","👍","👎","👌","✌️","🤞","🙏","💪","👀","🧠","🔥","✨","💥","🎉","✅","❌","⭐","⚠️"
]
RTL = ''.join([chr(c) for c in range(0x0590, 0x05CF)])  # Hebrew block subset
ACCENTS = "àáâãäåèéêëìíîïòóôõöùúûüÿçñÀÁÂÃÄÅÈÉÊËÌÍÎÏÒÓÔÕÖÙÚÛÜŸÇÑ"
MATH_SYMBOLS = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x2200, 0x2210))
BOX_DRAW = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x2500, 0x2520))
TYPICAL_WORDS = [
    "OpenCV", "Hershey", "Text", "Rendering", "fuzz", "测试", "テスト", "테스트", "пример", "δοκιμή",
    "مرحبا", "שלום", "नमस्ते", "🙂👍", "12345", "A_B-C.D/E", "(foo) [bar] {baz}", "αβγδε", "Ω≈ç√∫˜µ≤≥÷",
]

# Predefined templates to mix content patterns
TEMPLATES: List[str] = [
    "{words}",
    "{words}\n{words}",
    "{prefix}{ascii}",
    "{ascii}{suffix}",
    "{cjk}{cjk}{ascii}",
    "{emoji}{emoji}{words}",
    "{rtl}{ws}{words}",
    "{accents}{ws}{ascii}",
    "{box}{math}{ascii}",
    "{ascii}{nl}{ascii}{nl}{ascii}",
]

ESCAPES = ["%", "%%", "%d", "%s", "%f", "{", "}", "{{", "}}", "\\n", "\\t"]


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, s: str, k: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(s) for _ in range(k))


def _rand_emoji_seq(rng: random.Random, k: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(EMOJI) for _ in range(k))


def _bounded_len(rng: random.Random, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(lo, hi)


def _build_from_template(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    tpl = rng.choice(TEMPLATES)
    words = ' '.join(rng.choice(TYPICAL_WORDS) for _ in range(_bounded_len(rng, 1, 5)))
    ascii_part = _rand_choice(rng, ASCII_PRINTABLE, _bounded_len(rng, 5, 40))
    ws = _rand_choice(rng, WHITESPACES, _bounded_len(rng, 0, 8))
    cjk = _rand_choice(rng, CJK, _bounded_len(rng, 2, 16))
    emoji = _rand_emoji_seq(rng, _bounded_len(rng, 1, 8))
    rtl = _rand_choice(rng, RTL, _bounded_len(rng, 3, 12))
    accents = _rand_choice(rng, ACCENTS, _bounded_len(rng, 4, 20))
    math = _rand_choice(rng, MATH_SYMBOLS, _bounded_len(rng, 2, 10))
    box = _rand_choice(rng, BOX_DRAW, _bounded_len(rng, 2, 12))
    prefix = ''
    suffix = ''
    # Occasionally add control characters at start/end
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        prefix = _rand_choice(rng, CONTROL_ASCII, _bounded_len(rng, 0, 4))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        suffix = _rand_choice(rng, CONTROL_ASCII, _bounded_len(rng, 0, 4))
    # Occasionally add formatting-like tokens
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ascii_part = ascii_part + rng.choice(ESCAPES)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        words = words + rng.choice(ESCAPES)
    s = tpl.format(
        words=words,
        ascii=ascii_part,
        prefix=prefix,
        suffix=suffix,
        cjk=cjk,
        emoji=emoji,
        rtl=rtl,
        ws=ws,
        accents=accents,
        box=box,
        math=math,
        nl="\n",
    )
    return s


def _ensure_length_bytes(s: str, max_bytes: int, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) <= max_bytes:
        return s
    # Trim by bytes without breaking UTF-8: find a cut that decodes
    b = b[:max_bytes]
    # Back off until valid UTF-8
    end = len(b)
    while end > 0:
        try:
            return b[:end].decode('utf-8')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            end -= 1
    return ''


def _craft_edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Specific texts that stress font metrics and glyph coverage
    cases = [
        "",  # empty string
        " ",  # single space
        "\n\n\n",  # newlines
        "0" * rng.randint(1, 128),  # digits only
        "WMWMWMWMIlIlIlIl",  # tall/wide mixes
        "gypqjft|_",  # descenders/ascenders
        "Ångström – Café — ﬁ ﬂ",  # ligature-like and diacritics
        "مرحبا بالعالم",  # Arabic (RTL)
        "שלום עולם",  # Hebrew (RTL)
        "测试中文文本混合English123",  # Mixed CJK/Latin
        "🙂👍🔥✨🎉",  # pure emoji
        "\u200B\u200DZeroWidth and joiners",  # ZW chars in text
        "{0} %s %d %% {{ }}",  # braces and percent
    ]
    # Random long line of ASCII to test wrapping/trunc
    cases.append(_rand_choice(rng, ASCII_PRINTABLE, rng.randint(50, 200)))
    return cases


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose strategy: edge case or templated random mixture
    outputs: List[str] = []
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        outputs.extend(_craft_edge_cases(rng))
    # Add several templated variants
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        outputs.append(_build_from_template(rng))

    # Concatenate a subset with separators to form a single test string
    rng.shuffle(outputs)
    take = rng.randint(1, min(5, len(outputs)))
    sep_choices = [" ", "\n", "\n\n", "\t", " | "]
    sep = rng.choice(sep_choices)
    text = sep.join(outputs[:take])

    # Enforce maximum size
    text = _ensure_length_bytes(text, min(MAX_BYTES, 2048), rng)

    # Bias length to be within fuzzer stub caps (<=128 or <=64)
    # While keeping rich content; so trim further with some probability
    cap = 128 if rng.random() < 0.6 else 64
    text = _ensure_length_bytes(text, cap, rng)

    return text.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
